# External published nonlinear DAG learners vs our methods: edge-function accuracy (README_results)

Pre-registration: PLAN.md (commit c245cc1, before any run on the evaluation seeds). Raw rows: results/E1_d10_unif.csv, E3_d10_laplace.csv, E2_d20_unif.csv (10 datasets each, seeds 4000-4009, iSCM, mechanism m1, n=1000; 13 methods x 30 datasets = 390 rows, 0 errors). All tables below are generated by aggregate.py into results_summary.txt (full set, including R2, skeleton AUROC, own-graph counts, per-method timing). One CPU core, sequential.

## 1. Headline (read this first)
1. **An external method beats ours in part of the grid.** CAM-like (my Python reimplementation of the CAM recipe, not the original R code) has lower edge-function NRMSE than our best arm (BASILWs, chosen as pre-registered by pooled TOPK NRMSE) in the Laplace cell (0.151 vs 0.281, paired CI of the difference [0.061, 0.218], Wilcoxon p = 0.002, CAM-like better on 10/10 datasets), is lower at d=20 uniform (0.155 vs 0.211; CI [-0.005, 0.110], p = 0.084, so not significant; against the best arm in that cell, SSA 0.172, the gap is 0.017, a tie), and is slightly worse at d=10 uniform (0.176 vs 0.144, difference 0.031, CI [-0.014, 0.083], p = 0.625; CAM-like better on 6/10 datasets; verdict by the pre-registered rule: inconclusive, practically a tie). Pooled over the 30 datasets: CAM-like 0.161 vs BASILWs 0.212 (difference 0.052, CI [0.010, 0.096], p = 0.013; the 30 datasets are not independent because E1 and E3 share DAGs). Our family therefore does NOT win a head-to-head against a well-specified additive spline learner at d <= 20 on this benchmark. It ties or loses on edge functions, ties on AUROC (pooled difference -0.012, CI [-0.041, 0.012]), and ties on do-effects pooled (direct 0.168 vs 0.145, indirect 0.281 vs 0.236, both CIs include 0).
2. **Every neural / MLP-based published learner is far behind both CAM-like and all SPADE-family arms with selection** (per-cell TOPK NRMSE 0.69-0.94 vs 0.14-0.45 for the SPADE arms with selection and CAM-like; AUROC 0.54-0.71 vs 0.93-0.99; pooled orientation 0.45-0.59, near chance). Paired differences against our best arm: +0.51 to +0.61 NRMSE pooled, p = 0.002 (smallest attainable with 10 pairs) in every cell. This is the only place where the "external comparison" clearly favors us, and it is a comparison to methods whose published evaluations are structural, run here with default or repo settings and untuned (see limitations).
3. **The NAM-parameterised SPADE variant is worse than the spline version** in uniform cells (NAM-SSR minus SSR: +0.177 at d=10, +0.217 at d=20, both p <= 0.01) and better under Laplace noise (-0.092, p = 0.049). My pre-registered prediction (within 0.05) was wrong. The NAM variant was untuned (one hidden layer of 16 tanh units, 400 epochs, lr 1e-2), so this says only that this untuned NAM variant does not beat splines; it does not say NAM is worse in general.
4. Within our family at d <= 20, BASILWs is not better than SSR in the uniform cells (-0.023 at d=10, +0.008 at d=20, CIs include 0) and better under Laplace noise (-0.124, p = 0.010): the d=100 advantage of BASILWs over SSR in the earlier replication is not reproduced at these sizes except under heavy-tailed noise. SSA is a tie with SSR (pooled +0.004).
5. Amplitude calibration: CAM-like median slope 0.99-1.00 and BASILWs 0.93-1.00; SSC 0.43-0.69, NAM-SSC 0.20-0.54; all MLP learners 0.00-0.28 under TOPK (missed edges count as slope 0).

## 2. What was run
RUN (13 arms, 30 datasets, no failures): our SSC, SSA, SSR_k1.5, BASILWs (bench.run_method unchanged; SSA the adaptive branch), GAM-ridge (reference); external NOTEARS-MLP (repo PyTorch version), NOTEARS-MLP-gc (gcastle port of the original), DAGMA-nonlinear (dagma 1.1.1, repo call), DCE-like, GraN-DAG (gcastle 1.0.4 defaults), CAM-like (own implementation), NAM-SSC and NAM-SSR_k1.5 (NAM-parameterised SPADE variants, own implementation).
Status and reasons:
- NOTEARS-MLP (repo): RUN; this is the repo's own re-implementation (no l2 on the second layer), so its first-layer weight norm is not a scale-free edge strength; its RAW curves are decent (NRMSE 0.43 pooled) but the edge ranking is poor (AUROC 0.67). Not the original code.
- NOTEARS-MLP-gc: RUN (port of the original NOTEARS-MLP with L-BFGS-B).
- DAGMA-nonlinear: RUN with the repo's call (4000/8000 iterations; the library defaults use 50000/80000, 10x more; not run).
- DCE-like: RUN as a derivative-based post-hoc score on the DAGMA-MLP fit. Dagma-DCE proper (DCE inside the training objective): COULD NOT RUN, dagma 1.1.1 does not expose it. Its curves and do-effects are identical to DAGMA-nonlinear by construction.
- GraN-DAG: RUN (gcastle 1.0.4, defaults, 10000 iterations, no CAM pruning because gcastle does not provide it). It returns very sparse graphs (4.4-4.7 edges on average vs 10-20 true edges; 1.9-3.8 true positives).
- CAM-like: RUN, implemented in Python (greedy forward edge addition with BIC-penalised log-RSS gain, OLS B-spline terms, F-test pruning at p < 0.001). The original R CAM (mgcv GAMs): COULD NOT RUN (no R). Not claimed to be the original.
- NAM variants: RUN; NOT the original NAM (no ExU units, feature dropout, or deep per-feature networks) and not tuned.
- COULD NOT RUN, decided in advance: KAN-based Granger methods (time-series task), SCORE/NoGAM (structure only, no edge functions; already in earlier tables), a Sachs-based semi-synthetic arm (research/semisyn has no committed generator or results; not waited for).
Screening: at d=10, K=15 screening is vacuous (9 candidate causes per node); at d=20 it removes only the 4 lowest-ranked of 19 candidates per node (mild, not vacuous, contrary to the shorthand in the task description).


## 3. Tables (mean over datasets, sd over datasets in parentheses; lower NRMSE is better)
Rules (PLAN.md section 4): TOPK = oracle edge count k=|E|, missed true edges count NRMSE 1 (primary); OWN = the method's own graph (n/a for methods without selection); RAW = curves of the fitted model with no selection (how earlier SPADE results were scored). Our arms are scored under TOPK with the same code.

## 5. Verdicts against the pre-registered predictions (PLAN.md section 6)
- CAM-like matches or beats ours (criterion: TOPK NRMSE within 0.03 of or below our best arm in at least 2 of 3 cells): MET. Lower by 0.130 (E3) and 0.056 (E2, vs pooled-best BASILWs) and 0.031 higher in E1 (just outside the 0.03 band, CI includes 0). The stated expectation of a weakness in orientation under Laplace noise was wrong: CAM-like orientation 0.97 in E3 vs BASILWs 0.92, SSC 0.78. Its AUROC is 0.954/0.985/0.959 (E1/E3/E2) vs BASILWs 0.989/0.940/0.932; BASILWs is better at d=10 uniform (+0.035, CI [0.014, 0.056]) and CAM-like at Laplace (+0.045, CI [0.000, 0.107]).
- MLP methods worse than ours on structure and edge NRMSE, DAGMA-nonlinear the best of them: structure part MET (AUROC 0.54-0.71, pooled orientation 0.45-0.59). "DAGMA-nonlinear the best of them" is only partly right: by TOPK NRMSE DCE-like (0.720) and DAGMA-nonlinear (0.722) are the best MLP arms; by AUROC NOTEARS-MLP and NOTEARS-MLP-gc (0.67-0.68) are better than DAGMA-nonlinear (0.58). No MLP arm came within 0.03 of our best arm in any cell.
- NAM-SSC like SSC; NAM-SSR within 0.05 of SSR: NOT MET (NAM-SSC is 0.22 worse than SSC in the uniform cells, 0.05 better in Laplace; NAM-SSR is 0.18-0.22 worse than SSR in uniform cells, 0.09 better in Laplace). Probable reasons (not tested): untuned lr/width/epochs for tanh subnetworks, and the group norm scaling sqrt(11) x RMS; the shrinkage of SSC (amplitude) is larger in the NAM version at d=20 (slope 0.20 vs 0.48).
- BASILWs vs SSR at small d: "may vanish or reverse": vanishes in uniform cells, persists under Laplace noise (see item 4 of section 1).
- Do-effects: CAM-like and SSR/SSA similar: roughly MET (direct 0.145 vs 0.205/0.209, indirect 0.236 vs 0.305/0.303 pooled; CAM-like is lower, not just similar); MLP methods worse: MET (do NRMSE 0.70-0.81 direct, 0.89-0.97 indirect, i.e. close to 1, the score of predicting no effect).

## 6. Interpretation and caveats
- The iSCM benchmark is additive with smooth one-dimensional mechanisms, which is exactly the model class of CAM-like, NAM and the spline family. The additive learners are matched to the truth, the MLP learners are not. The result that CAM-like is as good as or better than our best arm is a fair warning for the paper: the edge-function accuracy of the SPADE family at d <= 20 is not specific to it, and BASILWs' advantage over a plain refit (SSR) is small at d <= 20 outside Laplace noise. The large-d regime (d = 100-500) where our scaled pipeline was designed was not tested here, and CAM-like was not run at d >= 50 (its forward search fits O(d^2) models per sweep; at d=20 it takes 0.3 s, but nothing is claimed about larger d).
- Reimplementations (CAM-like, NAM, DCE-like) may differ from the originals in ways that matter; the repo NOTEARS-MLP differs from the original. External methods were run with default or repo settings and were not tuned on this generator, whereas the SPADE lg rule and k=1.5 were chosen on earlier validation seeds from the same generator family; the MLP-method gap is therefore an upper bound on their disadvantage and should not be quoted as "published methods fail".
- OWN rule thresholds (0.3, 0.1) are conventions; TOPK and RAW do not depend on them. TOPK gives every method the oracle edge count; OWN is the deployable rule and gives the same conclusions (table above).
- 10 datasets per cell; pooled rows count the E1/E3 DAGs twice. No claim beyond d <= 20, n = 1000, mechanism family m1, iSCM, uniform and Laplace noise, ER degree 2.
- Do-effect skipped pairs (std of true curve < 0.05): 15 in total, the same for every method. No do-effect error above 1.52 (NOTEARS-MLP-gc indirect max); no blow-ups. GAM-ridge has no do-effect (as in bench).
- Statistical note: the best-arm choice (BASILWs, CAM-like) was made on the evaluation data, symmetrically for both lists; paired-test p-values are not corrected for multiplicity (3 cells x 6 metrics); only the TOPK NRMSE row is the pre-registered primary.

## 7. Deviations from PLAN.md and code changes
- After the plan commit: (i) one-line fix in ext_bench.py so NAM arms re-run the SSC cache when the cached screening mask belongs to another dataset (affects resumed runs only; the evaluation ran from scratch, no resume occurred); (ii) aggregate.py and run_all.sh added. Nothing else changed.
- Cycle-breaking of cyclic own graphs (PLAN section 4) was applied silently by the code; the number of removed edges was not logged.
- Sachs-based arm not added (see section 2).
